title: Tenant Debt Reconciler & Progressive Backpressure Adapter for Deterministic Limiter Outages
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Problem statement:
When a centralized admission limiter (regional or global) experiences transient outages or prolonged slowdowns, we currently have two problems: 1) tenant-level issued credits (tokens) can be consumed inconsistently across regions causing unfair debt accumulation, and 2) downstream services either drop requests (hard drop) or open a circuit without a predictable catch-up strategy, which creates hard-to-debug customer SLO regressions.

Goal:
Design and implement a Tenant Debt Reconciler (TDR) and a Progressive Backpressure Adapter (PBA) that together: 1) enforce tenant fairness during bursts and partial limiter outages, 2) deterministically reconcile "debt" (admission deficits) after recovery, and 3) provide predictable SLO behavior with observability hooks and rollback tokens for higher-tier customers.

High-level approach:
- Progressive Backpressure Adapter (PBA): a local edge component (per-proxy) that applies a smoothed, SLO-aware admission curve instead of immediate hard rejects when the central limiter is unreachable or saturated. PBA uses decaying tenant credit windows and client-priority weights to accept a fraction of requests during degraded periods.
- Tenant Debt Reconciler (TDR): a control-plane worker that maintains compact debt ledgers (region+tenant alignment) and issues reconciled catch-up allowances after the limiter recovers. Debt reconciliation runs with safety limits to prevent sudden global surges and supports per-tenant opt-in for post-outage burst allowance.

Telemetry & SLOs:
- New metrics: tenant_debt_level, pba_accept_rate, tdr_reconcile_events, reconcile_backpressure_applied, reconcile_delay_ms.
- Alerting: SLO breach when pba_accept_rate < expected_smoothing_threshold for 3m and reconcile backlog grows > 5% of tenant monthly quota.
- Dashboard: per-tenant heatmap showing instantaneous debt vs allowed catchup budget.

Design tradeoffs and mitigation:
- Risk: granting catch-up tokens can cause thundering herd; mitigated by token-sweep windowing and per-tenant rate caps.
- Complexity: leads to cross-region state; we will keep TDR state compact (vector clock of last-ack sequence + accrued debt scalar) and rely on eventual reconciliation with conservative bounds.
- Ownership: TDR lives in control-plane (single logical service with regional replicas). PBA integrates into the existing admission proxy binary with a feature flag.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary: enable PBA in dev region with introspection endpoints and simulated limiter outages (local chaos).
2) Telemetry verification: ensure metrics align with simulated bursts and no customer-facing regressions.
3) Gradual enable: 5% of production edge traffic -> 25% -> 100% with TDR read-only shadow mode.
4) Enable active reconciliation after 4 weeks of stable telemetry.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for PBA admission curve math and tenant priority weighting.
- Integration: local-run with a fake limiter, simulate region partition and assert debt ledger invariants.
- Chaos: runbook-driven chaos tests during a maintenance window (simulate limiter stale leases and full crash).

Outcomes / Success criteria:
- During simulated limiter outages, tenant fairness (90th percentile relative accept rate between tenants with equal weights) remains within 10% of baseline.
- Reconciliation completes without causing >5% spike in service latency.
- No unplanned SLO regressions for P1 customers during canary stage.

notes: If PBA detects per-tenant request spikes above 2x baseline for >1m during reconciliation, it will push reconcile into staged windows to avoid feedback loops.
TDR state persisted in a compact protobuf and replicated to a regional replica with tombstone markers to avoid double-counting.
For dedicated customers we will optionally expose a per-tenant reconciliation opt-out controlled by account settings in Console.
